This batch researches both spellings together since both point to the operator branded stackinfra.com in sources fetched this session, but this batch does not merge or rewrite either operator field value, leaving that naming inconsistency on file for a future pass to resolve if desired. STACK Infrastructure was launched January 16, 2019, per a trade press article from datacenterdynamics.com fetched this session, by IPI Partners, described in that article as a joint venture between Iron Point and Iconiq Capital. The new company launched with eight data centers across six United States markets and about 100 MW of capacity, built from two predecessor portfolios, three facilities from Infomart Data Centers in Ashburn Virginia, Portland Oregon, and Silicon Valley California, which IPI Partners had acquired in March 2018 after Equinix bought Infomart own Dallas headquarters building earlier that year, and five facilities from T5 Data Centers, a company IPI Partners had separately backed since 2016, in Atlanta Georgia, Chicago Illinois, and the Dallas Fort Worth Texas area, with T5 Data Centers itself continuing to operate separately afterward with remaining sites in Los Angeles, Charlotte, Colorado Springs, New York, and Cork City Ireland. Brian Cox, previously chief executive of Infomart Data Centers, became STACK Infrastructure own chief executive. STACK Infrastructure own about page, fetched this session, describes the company as a partner designing, developing, and operating global digital infrastructure, and states a current footprint of 10 metro markets in the Americas, 5 in Asia Pacific, and 7 in EMEA, 22 markets in total, though each market can itself include multiple campuses, for example Silicon Valley alone contains 3 campuses and Milan alone contains 11. This registry already carried, prior to this session, one already complete row for an Atlanta, Georgia facility a prior pass in this registry had itself corrected from an operator field of T5 Data Centers to Stack Infrastructure based on a documented 2019 sale, and one already complete row for the New Albany, Ohio facility, one of the original eight launch data centers, both consistent with the acquisition history recorded here and both untouched by this batch. None of the operator own pages fetched this session for the facilities in this batch published a street address, so no row in this batch receives an address field, a reverse geocoding attempt on one representative coordinate this session was again throttled, consistent with a persistent throttle on that service observed repeatedly earlier in this same campaign. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, POR02, fetched this session, states a single building on a 15 acre site with 24 MW of capacity. The page did not provide a street address, square footage, or opening date.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR02 campus in Hillsboro has published 24 MW of IT capacity. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this represents roughly 600 racks. The facility consists of a single building on a 15-acre site. No opening date, street address, or total power consumption is published.

POR02 ranks ninth among Oregon's facilities with published capacity figures, which total 156.6 MW across eight sites in a state where 133 facilities are mapped but most publish no specifications. The campus represents 15 percent of Oregon's disclosed IT capacity.

The facility qualifications and current tenants are not published.
